## f06b9f1a5114

**Reproduced teaching shortcut; audited source unchanged.** Source SHA-256:
`56af20ca7bb7db47f5223e17958ead3414a4f451b67283d6112db7c24685ba3c`;
executed rule hash: `022fc4b19863`.

A plausible wrong rule is: **for every color with exactly two cells, paint the
border of their bounding box, even when the pair is collinear.** The intended
rule requires the two cells to differ in both row and column. All canonical
training colors are diagonal pairs, so the shortcut fits every canonical
demonstration.

The current generator can assemble an ambiguous production-order lesson. At
`difficulty=easy`, `seed=0`, sample indices `[1,2,3,4]`, the shortcut matches the
intended output on the first three consecutive demonstrations and differs on the
fourth-pair query. The query contains a collinear color-4 pair at `(8,0)` and
`(8,8)`: the intended rule leaves the two cells unchanged; the shortcut fills
the entire row segment between them. All four selected Racket outputs match the
independent intended mirror.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/f06b9f1a5114/collinear-shortcut.json` — exact four inputs,
  intended/rival outputs, search parameters, source hash, and Racket verification.
- `checks/audit/f06b9f1a5114/inputs.json` — replay inputs.
- `checks/audit/f06b9f1a5114/racket.json` — official selected-rule outputs.
- `checks/audit/f06b9f1a5114/find_collinear_shortcut.py` — bounded reproducer.

Suggested future repair: declare the collinear-filter rival and schedule at least
one collinear negative witness in every actual three-demo lesson window. A
singleton negative does not refute this shortcut. No source was modified and
this finding does not alter approval.
